raw_response:
I am getting old now, 68 already, so I do not chase fancy things. I farm 13.1 mu total, same wheat-maize rotation as around here. I only finished primary school, so I mostly do what has worked on my land and what I see in the village. Wheat and maize together are the safest for me. Wheat gives steady grain, and after wheat I put maize right in, no wasting land. We have a well, so if the rain is short I can still save the crop, but pumping water costs money, so I do not water too much. Some people in my family work outside, so field labor must be simple and timed well. I will keep the full 13.1 mu in wheat first, then full 13.1 mu in summer maize after harvest. For fertilizer, I would rather not cut too hard, because if the crop turns yellow or weak, yield loss hurts more than spending a bit extra. But I also cannot spend like the big farmers, so I use moderate amounts, close to what worked before.

For wheat, I will sow in early to mid October, using a common improved village variety that people nearby trust. I will put most fertilizer before sowing, then one more topdressing around jointing if the stand looks decent and moisture is there. I expect to irrigate about three times if the year is normal: once after sowing or before winter if soil is dry, once at jointing, and once around filling if spring rain is poor. For maize, after wheat harvest in June I will not delay. That turnaround is tight here, so I will clear the wheat and seed maize right away with light tillage or direct seeding if I can arrange it. Maize I also manage in a simple way: base fertilizer plus one topdress, and usually one or two irrigations depending on rain. Herbicide is worth it because labor is short; insecticide only if I actually see pressure. If the year is normal, wheat should give me around 420 kg per mu and maize around 480 kg per mu. That is good enough and steady.
